title: Rigveda 6.72: To Indra and Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 6.72: To Indra and Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 6.72 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Indra and Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 6, the family book of Bharadvāja. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 489r-489v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 6.72.1-3 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 1, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 489r
translation.original_text:
1indrā̍somā̱ mahi̱ tad vā̍m mahi̱tvaṁ yu̱vam ma̱hāni̍ pratha̱māni̍ cakrathuḥ | yu̱vaṁ sūrya̍ṁ vivi̱dathu̍r yu̱vaṁ sva1̱̍r viśvā̱ tamā̍ṁsy ahataṁ ni̱daś ca̍ ||
2indrā̍somā vā̱saya̍tha u̱ṣāsa̱m ut sūrya̍ṁ nayatho̱ jyoti̍ṣā sa̱ha | upa̱ dyāṁ ska̱mbhathu̱ḥ skambha̍ne̱nāpra̍thatam pṛthi̱vīm mā̱tara̱ṁ vi ||
3indrā̍somā̱v ahi̍m a̱paḥ pa̍ri̱ṣṭhāṁ ha̱tho vṛ̱tram anu̍ vā̱ṁ dyaur a̍manyata | prārṇā̍ṁsy airayataṁ na̱dīnā̱m ā sa̍mu̱drāṇi̍ paprathuḥ pu̱rūṇi̍ ||
translation.text:
1GREAT is this might of yours, Indra and Soma: the first high exploits were your own achievements. Ye found the Sun ye found the light of heaven: ye killed all darkness and the Gods' blasphemers.
2Ye, Indra-Soma, gave her light to Morning, and led the Sun on high with all his splendour. Ye stayed the heaven with a supporting pillar, and spread abroad apart, the Earth, the Mother.
3Ye slew the flood -obstructing serpent Vr̥itra, Indra and Soma: Heaven approved your exploit. Ye urged to speed the currents of the rivers, and many seas have ye filled full with waters.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 489r (numbered 10r by the scribe) (OPenn image 489, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 6.71.4 ‹-ayaḥ-hanuḥ yajataḥ mandra-jihvaḥ ā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 489v (numbered 10v by the scribe), begins in RV 6.72.4 ‹pakvam āmāsu antaḥ ni›. Verses 6.72.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 6.72.4-5 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 1, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 489v
translation.original_text:
4indrā̍somā pa̱kvam ā̱māsv a̱ntar ni gavā̱m id da̍dhathur va̱kṣaṇā̍su | ja̱gṛ̱bhathu̱r ana̍pinaddham āsu̱ ruśa̍c ci̱trāsu̱ jaga̍tīṣv a̱ntaḥ ||
5indrā̍somā yu̱vam a̱ṅga taru̍tram apatya̱sāca̱ṁ śrutya̍ṁ rarāthe | yu̱vaṁ śuṣma̱ṁ narya̍ṁ carṣa̱ṇibhya̱ḥ saṁ vi̍vyathuḥ pṛtanā̱ṣāha̍m ugrā ||
translation.text:
4Ye in the unripe udders of the milch-kine have set the ripe milk, Indra, thou, and Soma. Ye have held fast the unimpeded whiteness within these many-coloured moving creatures.
5Verily ye bestow, Indra and Soma, wealth, famed, victorious, passing to our children. Ye have invested men, ye Mighty Beings, with manly strength that conquers in the battle.
